content: 1. Amobarbital and Efavirenz: Amobarbital may reduce the plasma levels or therapeutic effects of efavirenz by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 enzyme metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is uncertain. Monitor patients closely. 2. Efavirenz and Anagrelide: Both drugs can prolong the QTc interval, increasing the risk of cardiac arrhythmias. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative therapies. 3. Anastrozole and Efavirenz: Anastrozole may increase the plasma levels or effects of efavirenz by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unclear. Monitor patients closely. 4. Apalutamide and Efavirenz: Apalutamide, a strong CYP3A4 inducer, can significantly reduce the plasma levels and efficacy of efavirenz. Avoid coadministration or use alternative drugs. If coadministration is necessary, monitor for loss of therapeutic effect. 5. Efavirenz and Apixaban: Efavirenz may reduce the plasma levels or effects of apixaban by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. No initial dose adjustment is required, but close monitoring is recommended. 6. Efavirenz and Apomorphine: Both drugs can prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 7. Efavirenz and Apremilast: Efavirenz may reduce the plasma levels or therapeutic effects of apremilast by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative therapies. Strong CYP inducers can significantly decrease systemic exposure to apremilast, potentially reducing its efficacy. 8. Efavirenz and Aprepitant: Efavirenz may reduce the plasma levels or effects of aprepitant by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Conversely, aprepitant may increase the levels or effects of efavirenz. The clinical significance is unclear. Monitor closely. 9. Efavirenz and Arformoterol: Both drugs can prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 10. Efavirenz and Aripiprazole: Efavirenz may reduce the plasma levels or effects of aripiprazole by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs can prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 11. Efavirenz and Armodafinil: Armodafinil may reduce the plasma levels or effects of efavirenz by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Efavirenz may also reduce the levels or effects of armodafinil. The clinical significance is unclear. Monitor closely. 12. Efavirenz and Arsenic Trioxide: Both drugs can prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 13. Efavirenz and Artemether: Both drugs can prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative therapies. 14. Efavirenz and Artemether/Lumefantrine: Efavirenz may reduce the plasma levels or effects of artemether/lumefantrine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially reducing antimalarial efficacy. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative therapies. Both drugs can prolong the QTc interval. 15. Efavirenz and Asenapine: Both drugs can increase sedation and prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative therapies. 16. Efavirenz and Atazanavir: Efavirenz may reduce the plasma levels or effects of atazanavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Atazanavir may increase the levels or effects of efavirenz. Both drugs increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative therapies. 17. Efavirenz and Atidarsagene Autotemcel: Antiretroviral medications, including efavirenz, may interfere with the manufacturing of atidarsagene autotemcel. Discontinue antiretroviral therapy at least one month before cell mobilization and until all apheresis cycles are completed. 18. Efavirenz and Atogepant: Efavirenz may reduce the plasma levels or effects of atogepant by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust the atogepant dosage to 30 mg or 60 mg daily when coadministered with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inducers. Monitor closely. 19. Efavirenz and Atomoxetine: Both drugs can prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 20. Efavirenz and Atorvastatin: Efavirenz may reduce the plasma levels or effects of atorvastatin by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 21. Efavirenz and Atovaquone: Efavirenz may reduce the plasma levels of atovaquone through an unspecified mechanism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative therapies. 22. Efavirenz and Avanafil: Efavirenz may reduce the plasma levels or effects of avanafil by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 23. Efavirenz and Avapritinib: Efavirenz may reduce the plasma levels or effects of avapritinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs can increase sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. 24. Efavirenz and Axitinib: Efavirenz may reduce the plasma levels or effects of axitinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative therapies. 25. Efavirenz and Azithromycin: Both drugs can prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative therapies. 26. Efavirenz and Bazedoxifene/Conjugated Estrogens: Efavirenz may reduce the plasma levels or effects of bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 27. Efavirenz and Bedaquiline: Efavirenz may reduce the plasma levels or effects of bedaquiline by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially reducing its therapeutic efficacy. Both drugs can prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative therapies. 28. Efavirenz and Belumosudil: Efavirenz may increase the plasma levels or effects of belumosudil by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Increase the belumosudil dosage to 200 mg twice daily when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inducers. Monitor closely. 29. Efavirenz and Belzutifan: Belzutifan may reduce the plasma levels or effects of efavirenz by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. If coadministration is unavoidable, consider increasing the dose of the CYP3A4 substrate as clinically appropriate. Monitor closely. 30. Efavirenz and Benzhydrocodone/Acetaminophen: Efavirenz may reduce the plasma levels or effects of benzhydrocodone/acetaminophen by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs can increase sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. 31. Efavirenz and Betibeglogene Autotemcel: Antiretroviral medications, including efavirenz, may interfere with the manufacturing of betibeglogene autotemcel. Discontinue antiretroviral therapy at least one month before mobilization and until all apheresis cycles are completed. 32. Efavirenz and Bortezomib: Efavirenz may reduce the plasma levels or effects of bortezomib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 33. Efavirenz and Bosentan: Efavirenz may reduce the plasma levels or effects of bosentan by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Bosentan may also reduce the levels or effects of efavirenz. The clinical significance is unclear. Monitor closely. 34. Efavirenz and Bosutinib: Efavirenz may reduce the plasma levels or effects of bosutinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative therapies. 35. Efavirenz and Brentuximab Vedotin: Efavirenz may reduce the plasma levels or effects of brentuximab vedotin by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 36. Efavirenz and Brexanolone: Both drugs can increase sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. 37. Efavirenz and Brexpiprazole: Efavirenz may reduce the plasma levels or effects of brexpiprazole by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs can increase sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. 38. Efavirenz and Brigatinib: Efavirenz may reduce the plasma levels or effects of brigatinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially reducing its efficacy. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative therapies. 39. Efavirenz and Brimonidine: Both drugs can increase sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. 40. Efavirenz and Brivaracetam: Both drugs can increase sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. 41. Efavirenz and Bromocriptine: Efavirenz may increase the plasma levels of bromocriptine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially leading to vasospasm and ischemia. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative therapies. 42. Efavirenz and Buprenorphine: Efavirenz may reduce the plasma levels or effects of buprenorphine by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs can prolong the QTc interval. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative therapies. 43. Efavirenz and Bupropion: Efavirenz may reduce the plasma levels or effects of bupropion by inducing hepatic metabolism. Monitor closely. 44. Efavirenz and Buspirone: Efavirenz may reduce the plasma levels or effects of buspirone by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 45. Efavirenz and Butabarbital/Butalbital: Both drugs may reduce the plasma levels or effects of efavirenz by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance is unclear. Monitor closely. 46. Efavirenz and Cabazitaxel: Efavirenz may increase the plasma levels or effects of cabazitaxel by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 47. Efavirenz and Cabergoline: Efavirenz may increase the plasma levels of cabergoline by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially leading to vasospasm and ischemia. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative therapies. 48. Efavirenz and Cabozantinib: Efavirenz may reduce the plasma levels or effects of cabozantinib by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or consider alternative therapies. 49. Efavirenz and Calcifediol: Efavirenz may reduce the plasma levels or effects of calcifediol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely. 50. Efavirenz and Cannabidiol: Efavirenz may increase or decrease the plasma levels of cannabidiol by affecting CYP3A4, CYP2C19, and CYP2B6 metabolism. Adjust therapy and monitor closely.
